title: Carn A'Choire Mhoir Whitley Memorial

external_narratives.summary: IWM records the cairn memorial at the crash site of Whitley N1498 on Carn a Choire Mhoir, near Tomatin in the Highlands. The memorial commemorates personnel killed when the aircraft of 19 OTU crashed on 6 January 1942.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed crash site documentation of Whitley Mk.V N1498 from 19 OTU RAF Kinloss. The pilot ignored the last bearing obtained before the crash.

Cairn erection near crash site: A cairn was erected near the Whitley N1498 air crash site with a plaque attached.
narrative: On 6 January 1942, Whitley Mk.V N1498 of No.19 Operational Training Unit flew into Carn a Choire Mhoir near Tomatin whilst on an evening training flight from RAF Kinloss. The aircraft descended through cloud into high ground; the pilot had ignored the last bearing obtained before the crash. Four crew were killed: P/O John George Irvine RNZAF (pilot), P/O John Graham Castling RNZAF (pilot), Sgt Cecil Spencer George DFM (pilot/instructor), and Sgt Cyril Wright Green (wireless operator/air gunner). Three crew were injured and survived: Sgt Charles Murray Edgehill (observer), Sgt Derek Pike (wireless operator/air gunner), and Sgt Edward Francis John Kane RCAF (wireless operator/air gunner). The rear turret was recovered by helicopter around 1976 and is now at the Midland Air Museum in Coventry.
